Following the model’s broad public availability—set against Mythos 5’s more restricted initial access for trusted partners with planned expansion into biomedical research—we observe that safety guardrails continue to constrain meaningful engagement with biological and chemical content, precisely the domains where structured, methodology-driven agentic workflows could deliver the greatest value in areas such as transcriptomics, biomarker discovery, evidence synthesis, and protocol design.

What can Claude Fable 5 actually do?

I'm finding out in public 👇

🧠 15 days. 15 projects. 1 per day — all built with Fable.

Day 1 is live: my portfolio with a neural net you can train in your browser
→ https://t.co/LICdumNiVy

#15DaysOfFable #buildinpublic

How do you program agency?

It’s a question I’ve been slightly obsessed with for the past few months. I’ve built automations that wake up every morning and ask me what’s on my mind. I’ve wired agents to monitor the news and text me when something interesting happens. I’ve been building an eval agent that gathers feedback on its own work and builds a backlog of what to do next.

I’m not alone. Boris Cherny, who runs Claude Code at Anthropic, half-jokes that his main job now is to write the loops that prompt Claude. 

Addy Osmani named the discipline: loop engineering. Design a system that discovers work, executes it, verifies the results, updates its own instructions, and repeats. Give an agent goals, skills, and permission to spin up subagents. Then let it loose while you go do something else (like doom scroll).

At least that’s the pitch. In practice, my loops meander constantly. Token costs balloon. Agents get stuck. One bad decision dominos until the system is grinding away, very confidently, in the wrong direction. And every time, I wondered if it was because the model isn’t smart enough. Maybe wait for the next release.

I think our recent obsession with loop engineering made me lean more towards

better models != better outcomes 

better systems = better outcomes

A loop is really a collection of jobs: 

• Orchestration
• Memory
• Verification
• Retrieval
• Routing

In practice, it could look something like this:

• Automations discover new work.

• Worktrees allow multiple agents to operate in parallel.

• Skills capture project-specific knowledge.

• Connectors give agents access to real systems.

• Sub-agents verify each other’s work.

• Persistent memory keeps state between runs.

Frontier intelligence matters most in two places: 

1/ orchestration, knowing when to break a problem apart or when to stop, and 

2/ self-modification, where the system rewrites its own instructions 

Roughly fewer than 10 percent of the tasks in my loops genuinely need frontier reasoning. The rest need better systems: memory design, retrieval structure, verification gates, context architecture. 

How does this change the economics of the frontier, which seem increasingly resource-intensive to create? 

Frontier intelligence is valuable and scarce. But increasingly it seems like moat it really has is a short window of time. 

Distillation dupes frontier capability within months at a fraction of the cost. 

The labs know this. This week, when Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5, it did so with anti-distillation defenses engineered into the model itself. Suspected distillation attempts get rerouted to an older model. Requests related to frontier model development were quietly degraded by invisible safeguards, a choice the company walked back after backlash. 

They care because their edge is temporal. While open models will likely never be first (they don’t have the copious amount of proprietary user data), they can always catch up to the latest, sometimes in weeks. 

This is maybe what makes the frontier race a finite game. 

Each generation is a round: ship the model, monetize the premium window, watch the capability get replicated, ship again. The labs can never stop playing. And the rounds get harder to win profitably. 

The volume underneath, meanwhile, explodes. And everyone starts feeling the burn of cost. Citadel’s Economics of Intelligence report goes into how AI adoption is becoming less about what models can do and more about the price of running them at scale. 

A lot of VC doomisms seems to be about how the frontier models are just going to build it all and that there’s nothing left to build. I think it’s the opposite: the frontier intelligence race will stay scarce and valuable. But it is playing a finite game: the labs have to win every round to stay in it.

I think the better position to be in would be those building the inference engineering infrastructure that runs underneath it all.

quotedTweet.text:
anthropic shipped claude fable 5 yesterday, and the headline isn't a benchmark. it's that their most capable public model now ships with a governor that silently routes a slice of your sessions to a weaker model, and you don't get to see which ones.

here is what is actually known so far.

two products, one set of weights.
fable 5 is the public release. mythos 5 is the same underlying model with the safeguards lifted in some areas, gated to cyber defenders and infrastructure providers through project glasswing, run with the US government. anthropic calls mythos the strongest cybersecurity model in the world, which is most of the reason you can't have it.

the safety router is an architecture decision, not a disclaimer.
on sensitive topics fable 5 quietly answers from claude opus 4.8 instead. anthropic says this triggers in under 5% of sessions and is tuned conservatively, so it will catch harmless requests too. if you are building evals or agents on top, your p95 capability is no longer the model you think you bought.

the capability claims, with names attached.
stripe ran a codebase-wide migration on a 50-million-line ruby codebase in a single day. their by-hand estimate was over two months for a full team.
hebbia says it is the first model past 90% on their analytics benchmark, a 10-point jump over opus.
on a frontier physics eval, one lab got in 36 hours roughly where gpt-5.5 landed after four days, using a third of the reasoning tokens.

the long-horizon work is the actual story.
mythos 5 ran about a week of largely autonomous genomics: assembled single-cell data across 138 species, trained its own model, and beat a model published in science while being 100x smaller. on drug design it moved about 10x faster than the manual process, and its molecular-biology hypotheses were preferred around 80% of the time over opus-class models.

the price: $10 per million input tokens, $50 per million output. under half of what mythos preview cost.

the part to sit with: the most capable model you can rent now has a built-in policy layer that downgrades part of your traffic by design. capability went up. so did the number of things standing between your prompt and the answer.

· 今日 X 上的 AI 舆情小结

今天 X 平台上有关 AI 的讨论主线是，AI 能力正从代码生成向全流程自动化运维拓展，同时伴随便利性升级和商业化、文化认同的激烈碰撞。共识主要体现在开发者对更灵活的 API 速率配额管理、AI 编码助手的能力提升以及自动化仓库维护降本增效的前景普遍持欢迎态度，并认可特斯拉 Full Self-Driving 在乘坐体验上的快速迭代。分歧则围绕这些更新展开，不少用户质疑 Codex “储蓄重置”能否真正解决高强度限流的痛点，Claude Code 与 Cursor、Copilot 的编码能力孰优孰劣尚无定论，开源仓库维护 agent 的安全性、可靠性以及 AI 上市公司的正式着装究竟是背离创新精神还是走向成熟，都引发了针锋相对的观点。潜在风险在于，AI 自主代码修改可能带来安全责任归属模糊与治理冲突，模糊的定价策略和商业分层可能侵蚀开发者信任，而自动驾驶仍面对安全性怀疑和文化转型若过于剧烈也可能削弱行业的创新活力。

🔹 💡 大佬观点(Influencer Insights)

📢 AI 行业日报：端侧模型爆发与 Agent 工程化深水区

🔹 一、今日核心热点：三大技术趋势

▫️ 1. **端侧模型（On-device Model）进入实用临界点**

多位博主密集验证端侧模型的生产力价值，标志着该领域从"技术演示"迈向"日常可用"：

• @zhixianio 展开"苦行僧式修行"：使用 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ6-fp16-mtp 模型，通过 oMLX 运行 Native MTP，在 PA（OpenClaw）和 Coding 场景下，响应速度超越远程 LLM，且"智商在线，还能帮我多想多做一步"。他甚至用 Mac 跑端侧模型来"解冻饭团"——看似玩笑，实则验证端侧推理的实时性已可支撑物理世界交互。

• Google Gemma 4 系列成为焦点：@zhixianio 密集测试 Gemma 4 的 QAT（量化感知训练）版本、12B 多模态模型，评价其"日文邮件解析分类入库"性能不错，但指出中文音频识别"驴唇不对马嘴"、英文和日语表现优异。他特别提到 QAT 是"新的端侧模型优化思路"——训练阶段即假设会被量化，以此提升后续量化效果。

• 端侧 TTS 应用落地：@zhixianio 的播客《认知有县》E5 引入 Owlia（端侧 TTS）作为主持人，本身就是端侧模型的应用案例。

> 洞察：端侧模型的竞争已从"能不能跑"转向"跑得好不好、省不省、快不快"。Google 的 QAT、Apple 的 MLX 生态、阿里的 Qwen 系列正在形成三足鼎立。

▫️ 2. **Claude Fable 5：能力跃升与成本焦虑并存**

Anthropic 的 Fable 5 成为今日最具争议性的产品，呈现"技术惊艳"与"经济不可持续"的张力：

| 维度 | 观察 |
|------|------|
| 能力边界 | @zhixianio：40 分钟完成 70% 工作，还指出设计不合理之处；@dotey：Fable 5 完成复杂功能（导入 Figma 本地文件、重建设计系统），"没有 Fable 5 帮忙搞不定" |
| 时间/成本 | @Pluvio9yte：速度"像乌龟慢爬"，消耗为 Opus 的 1.5x；@dotey 引用案例：团队成员 10 小时消耗等值 $1,500；@vista8：Fable 5 思考 15 分钟才开始行动 |
| 使用策略 | @Pluvio9yte 建议开 `/effort max` 强度；@dotey 则因 Token 消耗"不敢随便选 Max" |

> 关键分歧：@Pluvio9yte 认为 Fable 5 是"Opus4.6++与 GPT-5.5++的结合版"，未到"非常惊艳"；而 @zhixianio 直呼"Shut up and take my money"。这种分歧反映了用户场景差异——前端 Demo 类任务 vs. 复杂工程化任务。

▫️ 3. **Agent 工程化：从 Vibe Coding 到 Contract First**

行业对 AI 编程的认知正在深化，从"炫技"进入"工程纪律"阶段：

• @Pluvio9yte 提出 "Contract First" 最佳实践："没有定义好契约，其他一切都是空谈"。他基于 OpenSpec 二开形成开发框架，将"全栈开发中容易漂移的上下文外化成契约，让人和 AI 都有稳定参照物"。

• @dotey 系统总结 Claude Design 经验：强调 Design System 防"AI 味"、Markup 局部修改、CLAUDE.md 上下文管理、单向同步流程（Design → Code）。

• @vista8 开发 "乔木 Goal Meta Skill" 和 "乔木 AI PRD Skill"，将"一句话需求"转化为 AI 可执行的 Goal 指令和 PRD 文档，解决"人喜欢的 PRD 和 AI 喜欢的不一样"的问题。

> 趋势判断：Agent 编程正在形成新的工程范式——不是取代软件工程，而是放大软件工程的重要性（@dotey 引用观点）。

🔹 二、独特观点与行业前瞻

▫️ 1. **机器人"GPT-3 时刻"：因果世界模型 vs. VLA**

@AI_Jasonyu 转述黄碧薇（@huang_biwei）与极客公园的对谈，提出激进预测："明年初（2027），机器人就会有 GPT-3 时刻"。

核心论点：
• 现有 VLA + 堆数据路径"根本不通"——桌面高 2 厘米机器人就 fail
• 因果大模型将 scaling 斜率从 0.2 拉到 0.8，"几百个 demo 顶别人一万个"
• 世界模型三阶：渲染（Sora）→ 模拟（李飞飞）→ 想象（因果大模型）

Fable 5 is amazing in frontend. Few weeks ago prepared in  a new public pages layout for @dobrastrzelnica with Claude Design. Yesterday @claudeai Fable started implementing it. Today I spend 1-2 hours for the small corrections, testing and fixing missing points. https://t.co/6mTm7MlMvm

Fable 5 redesigned my onboarding experience. 

- 30 minutes of planning
- 2 hours to MVP
- ~2 additional hours of polish

The new experience is feeling really, really good and the model felt like the best Anthropic model I have worked with to date.

It wasn't perfect though. Even with 30 minutes of planning in Plan mode, it still made mistakes. Don't expect the code or feature to be fully baked in one or two prompts.

- Settings UI clipped
- It misunderstood 2 features requests and implemented things wrong
- It was creative with the UI design, but still not polished
- I went back and forth about 25 times
- It's slow for interactive development

I burned through ~20% of my Weekly usage and my entire 5 hour usage window.

I do think it's worth a shot, but it feels pricey compared to GPT-5.5, which feels unlimited to me.

We'll see tomorrow how GPT-5.5 performs with the same task ... and I guess ~4 hours of effort.

Is Fable 5 that much better at UI? I still had UI bugs, which you can see in the images attached. Getting the padding to look decent too several prompts.

Dialogue (girl, drained, comically breathless): 「あっつい〜…」

Shot 2 (2-4s): Follows Panel 3-4. She stops, then notices a glowing vending machine in the shade; her eyes lock onto one frosted can of "Fable". Camera: slow pan from her face to the vending machine. Lighting: cool blue glow from the machine against warm sunlight.
Dialogue (girl, hopeful gasp): 「…ん！？」

Shot 3 (4-7s): Follows Panel 5-7. Macro shot of the ice-cold "Fable" can dropping into the tray, condensation droplets flying; she presses it to her cheek with blissful relief, then the pull-tab opens with sparkling carbonation spray. Camera: fixed macro close-up. Lighting: crisp backlit product lighting, droplets glittering.

Shot 4 (7-10s): Follows Panel 8-9. She takes a big satisfying gulp, head tilted back against the deep blue sky, bubbles catching the light — then her eyes snap open, sparkling, energy surging back. Camera: low-angle push-in to her face. Lighting: brilliant summer sunlight, lens flare.
Dialogue (girl, explosive joyful shout, classic Japanese CM delivery): 「生き返るーっ！」

Shot 5 (10-13s): Follows Panel 10-11. Camera: fixed product close-up.
Lighting: clean bright studio-style commercial lighting.
Narration (warm male CM voice, pronounced fei-bu-ru): 「フェイブル。」
Text: "夏に、負けない。フェイブル"

① Claude Fable 5にストーリーボードジェネレーター制作を依頼

使用したプロンプトはこちら↓
-----------------
私は画像生成AIの「GPT Images 2.0」向けの、ストーリーボード画像を作れるプロンプトを作れるツールを作りたい。
要はストーリーボード向けプロンプトジェネレーターです。
生成するストーリーボードは、動画生成AI（Seedance 2.0）に参照させるのに使用します。

以下の項目を選択し、プロンプトを作れるツールを作ってください。
入力された情報をもとに、最終的にClaudeがGPT Images 2.0向けのプロンプトを生成するツール。

ストーリーボートのタイトル：※必須（ストーリーボートにタイトル名を表示させるか選択できるようにして）
映像の形式：※必須
ストーリー系
CM・広告系
教育・解説系
情報発信系
エンタメ系
アート・表現系
などを選択できるようにして。
ストーリー概要：概要を入力（ストーリー概要を入力したらエンハンスできる機能もつけて。もしここが空だったら、タイトル・形式を参考にして良い感じのストーリーを作って。）
スタイル：アニメ（日本の高品質アニメーション）・アニメ（ピクサー風）・実写・その他（フォームに記入）
パネル数：4〜20までを選択
パネルの形：正方形・横長・縦長を選択
パネルに数値を入れるか？：オンにするとパネルに数値が付与される
パネルに細かい情報を入れるか？：オンにすると、それぞれのパネルに「アクション」「カメラワーク」「セリフ」が記載される
キャラクターシートの有無：ストーリーボードにキャラクターシートを含める場合はチェック

何か不明な箇所や、細かく定義したい箇所があったら遠慮せず指摘して。

HOW TO PROMPT CLAUDE FABLE 5 (MYTHOS)
Plain English translation of Anthropic's official playbook
https://t.co/5G8pMdif1l — @aiedge_

WHAT MAKES FABLE 5 DIFFERENT — THINK OF IT AS A CONSULTANT, NOT A CHATBOT

• Multi-day runs — Sustains output over extended periods — built for autonomous work
• First-pass quality — Single-pass implementations that previously took days of iteration
• Asks clarifying Qs — Asks before kicking off autonomous runs — needs the why, not just the what
• 50+ subagents — Spins up parallel agents for complex tasks automatically
• Better vision — Dense charts, screenshots, web apps — substantially higher accuracy
• Coding genius — Especially powerful for codebase review, debug, and security audits

EFFORT LEVELS · MATCH TO TASK

• Low / Medium — Quick questions · simple rewrites · conversational
• High — Default for most tasks
• Xhigh — Complex builds · multi-step analysis · quality non-negotiable
• Ultracode — Full autonomous orchestration with Dynamic Workflows

TELL IT WHY, NOT JUST WHAT
Fable 5 needs context to connect the task to relevant information. Context lets it infer — not guess.

"I'm working on [larger task] for [who it's for]. They need [what the output enables]. With that in mind: [your actual request]."

KEEP INSTRUCTIONS SHORT
Counter-intuitive: over-engineering prompts degrades output. Fable 5 would have figured out the right approach on its own. A short brevity instruction beats listing every pattern.

OPTIMAL PROMPT STRUCTURE
Every high-quality Fable 5 prompt has 4 components:

"I'm working on [larger task] for [who it's for]. They need [what the output enables].
Request: [specific ask in one clear sentence]
Output format: [exactly how you want it structured]
Constraints: [what must not happen]"

/loop STRUCTURE
Lets Fable 5 work without manual intervention. Structure:

/loop <time interval> + goal
Example:
/loop 15 minutes, check if my build is passing, notify if it fails.
Stop:
/loop stop [loop name]

CHECKPOINT PROMPT
Define when Fable 5 should stop and check in with you:

"Pause for me only when the work genuinely requires my input: a destructive or irreversible action, a real scope change, or something only I can provide. Otherwise, keep going and report back when done."

MEMORY INSTRUCTION
Fable 5 performs better when it can record lessons from previous runs. Provide a markdown file and add this instruction:

"Store one lesson per file with a one-line summary at the top. Record corrections and confirmed approaches alike, including why they mattered. Don't save what the repo or chat history already records. Update an existing note rather than creating a duplicate. Delete notes that turn out to be wrong."

⚠️ 6 CAVEATS TO KNOW

• Runs longer than expected — Individual requests for hard tasks can run for many minutes at xhigh. Plan for it.
• Goes beyond what you asked — Fable 5 is proactive by design — can take unrequested actions. Use checkpoints.
• Old prompts may hurt — Skills or project instructions built for Opus 4.8 or earlier may produce worse results. Start fresh.
• Some requests will decline — Fable may decline prompts you think are safe — especially cybersecurity and life sciences.
• Can stop early — If it stops, just say 'go ahead and do it end-to-end' — that's enough.
• Tokens are expensive — Paid plans until June 22 — then API only. Always set max_budget_usd in loops.
